checklist.notes: The contrast, timings, role labels, and correction routine are explicit and easy to follow.
The stated 8+8+10+9 minute stages exactly fit the 35-minute allocation and keep the target narrow.
Perception, production, repair, and spoken interaction all serve the minimal-pair application goal.
The safe-detail exchange and friendly repair enact basic participation and combine the allocated A1.1 pronunciation and interaction capabilities.
The lesson moves from articulatory comparison through a model repair to recording and freer role-play.

The central success check is not independent: the learner records a known four-word sequence, later recalls/identifies that same sequence, and has no external or keyed reference capable of showing whether the produced contrast is intelligible.
Multiple cues, slow-to-normal rehearsal, and non-deficit retry language support an individual learner without making population-wide claims.

findings.description: ‘Record, wait, and identify’ confounds memory, intended production, and perception. A learner can recover the intended order even when the recording does not contain a reliable /ɪ/–/iː/ contrast, so the stated success check cannot establish its target.
findings.recommendation: Provide an independently randomized/keyed listening source for perception and a genuinely independent intelligibility check for production, or label self-recording only as rehearsal rather than evidence of success.
